classification.difficultyReason: Interpret the water surface as a chord in a semicircular cross-section and calculate its length.

content.prompt:
A hemispherical bowl has a diameter of $10\text{ cm}$.
Water is poured into the bowl until its surface is $3\text{ cm}$ below the top of the bowl as shown.
Find the diameter of the water surface.

spec.description: Upward-opening semicircular bowl, dashed rim diameter, horizontal water surface, and vertical double-headed 3 cm depth arrow.
spec.mathematics: Bowl radius is 5 cm; water surface is 3 cm below the centre-level rim.
spec.answerVisibility: The water diameter is not labelled or supplied.

answer.worked:
The bowl's radius is $5\text{ cm}$. The perpendicular from the centre to the water surface bisects its diameter. Let $x$ be half the water diameter.
$$\begin{align*}x^2+3^2 &= 5^2\\x^2 &= 16\\x &= 4\text{ cm}\\\text{Water diameter} &= 2\times4=8\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$
